policy: Append-only contextual re-review, separate from legacy ledger. Decisions apply to individual labels under the documented rubric; not human-review or delivery-effectiveness evidence.

rubric.unclassified: A retrieval fallback, not a positive speech-function category. A false support flag means it is not admitted as a substantive pattern, not that the passage lacks meaning or the fallback was computed incorrectly. Record contextual function in subtype without silently adding candidate labels; these cases cannot estimate recall.
rubric.contrast_or_disagreement: Explicit opposition or change between propositions/events; subtype need not be interpersonal disagreement.
rubric.story_or_personal_experience: A personally attributed event placed in a narrative sequence.
rubric.question: An interrogative or explicitly narrated self-question; no audience response implied.
rubric.uncertainty_or_qualification: Explicit qualification of a claim, prediction or interpretation; hypothetical ability alone is insufficient.
rubric.call_to_action: A present substantive action appeal directed to an audience, including collective proposals and broad encouragement. Embedded advice to a story character, conversational turn allocation and procedural stage management are excluded. A promotional outro can contain an action appeal, but its speaker attribution must remain separate from the featured speech. Support concerns discourse function, not effectiveness or endorsement.
rubric.definition: Explains a term or phrase through a translation, paraphrase, or concrete unpacking of its intended content. Merely inferring a consequence, assigning significance, or interpreting a symptom/event does not establish a definition. Operational reformulation is distinguished from lexical definition.
rubric.conclusion_or_summary: A local or whole-speech takeaway that compresses, generalizes, or draws a closing inference from identifiable preceding material. It need not end a speech. A connector or new topic announcement alone is insufficient. Record local versus broad function; no truth or effectiveness endorsement.
rubric.example: A concrete member, case, comparison, quantity or imagined scenario linked to an identifiable broader point. Distinguish enumeration, illustration and asserted evidence. A marker alone, bare advice or vivid story detail without a local general-to-case relation is insufficient. Support describes discourse function, not factual truth or effectiveness.
